did_you_know.text: Psalm 33 opens with a call for the righteous and upright to rejoice and praise the Lord; such praise is presented as fitting for them.
The psalm mentions several forms of musical accompaniment: the lyre, the ten-stringed harp—a ten-stringed instrument—as well as singing and joyful shouts.
The psalm connects the uprightness of the Lord’s word with the faithfulness of his works: his word is upright, and all he does is done faithfully.
Righteousness, justice, and steadfast love appear together as qualities associated with the Lord, and his steadfast love is described as filling the earth.
The creation of the heavens and their host is attributed to the word of the Lord and the breath of his mouth, expressing his creative power.
The verse emphasizes the power of God’s word: the Lord spoke, and it came to be; he commanded, and it stood firm.
The plans of individuals and nations may change or come to nothing, but the Lord’s counsel is described as standing forever.
The Lord is described as the one who forms the hearts of all people and understands all their works; therefore, his oversight includes both their inner thoughts and their actions.
The psalm teaches that military power alone cannot guarantee deliverance: neither a king, a warrior, nor a horse can be saved by strength alone.
The psalm’s hope rests on fearing the Lord and waiting for his steadfast love; the Lord is described as the helper and shield of those who wait for him.
